dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agency personnel involved in the program and State, local, Tribal, and territorial partners who utilize its threat assessment services.
dimensions.evidence: equipping State, local, Tribal, and territorial (SLTT) partners to identify, assess, and report threats of targeted violence.

dimensions.assessment: Reorganizes administrative housing and funding sources for an existing program, ensuring continuity of operations without reducing capabilities.
dimensions.evidence: The transfer under this subsection shall not result in the reduction of capabilities or services provided to SLTT partners by the NTER Program.

dimensions.assessment: Prohibits the use of National Intelligence Program funds and mandates the identification of alternative non-NIP funding sources.
dimensions.evidence: no funds appropriated or otherwise made available under the National Intelligence Program may be obligated or expended for the NTER Program

dimensions.assessment: Shifts administrative oversight of a specific program between two internal DHS offices and mandates alternative funding mechanisms and periodic reporting.
dimensions.evidence: transfer the National Threat Evaluation and Reporting Program to OSLLE from I&A.

dimensions.assessment: Enforces a permanent prohibition on NIP funding and establishes a permanent administrative transfer alongside periodic reporting requirements over a two-year window.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Homeland Security shall transfer the National Threat Evaluation and Reporting Program

missing_information: The exact dollar amounts currently allocated under the National Intelligence Program to the NTER Program
Specific alternative non-NIP funding lines to be utilized
importance_detail.rationale: The bill transfers the National Threat Evaluation and Reporting Program within the Department of Homeland Security from the Office of Intelligence and Analysis to the Office for State and Local Law Enforcement, while prohibiting the use of National Intelligence Program funds for the program. This shifts internal departmental responsibilities and funding streams without altering the underlying program mission.
